headline_status_explanation: The theorem is kernel-checked by Lean 4, but the dependency closure currently contains seven `True`-typed axioms (three bridge + three crypto-shape + the Lean kernel built-ins that ARE genuine TCB). The bridge axioms therefore provide NO semantic constraint on the deployed bytecode — they are documentation markers in `#print axioms`. The cryptographic-content axiom `EUF_CMA_SPHINCSplusC` does have real propositional content (directly asserts non-forgery), and the kernel built-ins are universally trusted. The `entrypoint_honest` axiom has content but states a property of a Lean fiction (`Bridge.EntryPoint.handleOp`), not the deployed EntryPoint v0.6 at the canonical address. See the plan at `contracts/verification/docs/DISCHARGE_PLAN.md` for the discharge roadmap.

discharge_states.placeholder: Lean type reduces to `True` — axiom has no semantic content. Hostile removal of the axiom would not break the proof.
discharge_states.misleading: Axiom has real content but states a property of a Lean model that is not formally connected to the deployed bytecode.
discharge_states.cited-tcb: Axiom has real content; the discharge is a citation to a peer-reviewed proof or universally-trusted Ethereum infrastructure.
discharge_states.discharged: Axiom has real content; a machine-checkable artifact (Kontrol session ID, Certora rule-set hash, Lean proof term) discharges it.
discharge_states.kernel-tcb: Lean 4 kernel built-in. Trusted as part of the kernel's soundness.

axioms.name: SphincsCVerify.Bridge.EntryPoint.entrypoint_honest
axioms.description: If `handleOp` (Lean model of EntryPoint v0.6) decreases the wallet's balance, then `validateSignature` returned `Result.success`.
axioms.lean_type_today: ∀ σ op effects, (handleOp σ op effects).balance σ.walletAddress < σ.balance σ.walletAddress → validateSignature ... = (Result.success, _)
axioms.status_detail: Axiom has real propositional content but its subject is the Lean `handleOp` function defined in the same file — not the deployed EntryPoint v0.6 at 0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789. As stated, the axiom is provable from the def of `handleOp`; its real role is to document the assumption that the real EntryPoint behaves the same way as the Lean fiction.
planned_discharge: tier-1.7: rename to `LeanEntryPointModel.handleOp` to make the abstraction explicit

tier-3: Kontrol against deployed EntryPoint v0.6 mainnet bytecode at 0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789, proving the three properties (wallet_executed_only_after_validate_success, entrypoint_never_directly_debits_wallet, userOpHash_per_v0.6_spec)
fallback if Kontrol intractable: codehash-pin + cite ERC-4337 v0.6 reference source

axioms.name: SphincsCVerify.Crypto.EUF_CMA_SPHINCSplusC
axioms.description: SPHINCS+C10 is EUF-CMA secure: no PPT adversary produces a forgery against a fresh verifying key after at most Q signing-oracle queries, except with probability ε(A) + Q·2^-128.
axioms.lean_type_today: SM_DT_TCR_F_Shape → ITSR_F_Shape → hMsg_RO_Shape → ∀ vk transcript msg* sig*, isForgery vk transcript msg* sig* → False
axioms.status_detail: Axiom has real content (asserts non-forgery), but the three preconditions reduce to `True` (see SM_DT_TCR_F, ITSR_F, hMsg_random_oracle below). The Lean axiom is the cited result; the discharge is the EasyCrypt mechanization plus the SPHINCS+ → SPHINCS+C transition argument.
planned_discharge: tier-4: replace `True`-typed preconditions with concrete advantage-bound shapes (no full Lean mechanization of EUF-CMA)
cited as: Barbosa/Dupressoir/Hülsing/Meijers/Strub ASIACRYPT 2024 (SPHINCS+) + Hülsing PQC2022 (+C variant)
axioms.citation: Barbosa, Dupressoir, Hülsing, Meijers, Strub. 'A Tight Security Proof for SPHINCS+, Formally Verified.' IACR ePrint 2024/910, ASIACRYPT 2024, LNCS 15487. SPHINCS+C variant: Hülsing et al. 'SPHINCS+C: Compressing SPHINCS+ With (Almost) No Cost.' NIST PQC2022. Tight bound: Hülsing, Kudinov. 'Recovering the tight security proof of SPHINCS+.' ASIACRYPT 2022.
